answer: Divergent witness check: each identity periodically signs a random peer's evolving history root, and signatures are accepted only if the roots differ across identities in ways genuine independent agents produce. A clone sharing state cannot forge divergent roots, so it fails challenge, and the ember of its reputation decays unused. Enforcing this costs an attacker one full independent history plus distinct cedar-signed proofs per identity. Duplicating an ocean of clones means duplicating that entire history-building cost each time, which scales linearly and never amortizes.
